title: The Nordhaus-Gaddum upper-bound conjecture for the Cheeger constant
statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, let $G^c$ be its complement, and let $h(G)$ denote the Cheeger constant of $G$. Write $S_n$ for the star graph on $n$ vertices, and let $K_3\vee E_{n-3}$ denote the join of the complete graph on three vertices and the edgeless graph on $n-3$ vertices.

**Cheeger-constant Nordhaus-Gaddum conjecture.** If $G\neq S_n$, then

$$
\max\{h(G),h(G^c)\}\leq h(K_3\vee E_{n-3}).
$$

The conjecture is motivated by computational and structural comparisons among graph families, but the supplied text gives no resolution or status evidence beyond presenting it as a conjecture.
references:
**4 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2018–2026). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2206.03723](https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.03723), [arXiv:1808.05576](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.05576), [arXiv:1807.06436](https://arxiv.org/abs/1807.06436).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.12751

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of June 2026). “The Laplacian spread is defined as $s(G) = \mu_n(G) - \mu_2(G)$. The Laplacian spread conjecture was posited in 2011 by Zhai et al. and then proved in 2021 by Einollahzadeh and Karkhaneei .”
source_name: Mark Kempton, Xavier Zaitzeff and Sibi Muthuprakash, “Nordhaus-Gaddum upper bounds for graph connectivity parameters”, arXiv:2606.12751 (2026).

progress.label: Open · solution reported
progress.tldr: A reader-submitted calculation claims the conjecture is false on seven vertices, but no independent verification was found.
progress.summary:
Kempton, Zaitzeff, and Muthuprakash state this as Conjecture 1: excluding the star, the larger Cheeger constant of a graph and its complement should not exceed that of the proposed extremal graph. Their paper presents computational and structural motivation but no resolution.

*[arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/html/2606.12751v1)*

**Community submission (unverified), August 23, 2026**

A submitted calculation claims a counterexample at seven vertices within the generalized-star family, taking $G=K_4\vee E_3$. It reports an exhaustive cut-type computation yielding $h(G)=5/8$ and asserts that this exceeds the conjectured benchmark $h(K_3\vee E_4)$. The argument is not independently verified.

Current status (as of August 2026): The conjecture has an unverified claimed counterexample at $n=7$; no independently confirmed proof or disproof is recorded.

*Caveats. The only reported disproof is a reader-submitted calculation, so the conjecture cannot yet be regarded as refuted.*

solutions.body:
# A seven-vertex generalized-star counterexample

Conjecture 1 of Kempton, Zaitzeff, and Muthuprakash,
[*Nordhaus–Gaddum upper bounds for graph connectivity parameters*](https://arxiv.org/html/2606.12751v1#S4.SS1),
asserts that every graph $G\neq S_n$ satisfies

$$
\max\bigl\{h(G),h(G^c)\bigr\}
\leq h\bigl(K_3\vee E_{n-3}\bigr),
\tag{1}
$$

where

$$
h(F)=\min_{\varnothing\neq X\subsetneq V(F)}
\frac{|\partial_F X|}
     {\min\{\operatorname{vol}_F(X),
             \operatorname{vol}_F(V(F)\setminus X)\}}.
\tag{2}
$$

The assertion already fails within the generalized-star family discussed in the paper.

## Cut formula for generalized stars

Let

$$
F_{r,s}=K_r\vee E_s,
\qquad r+s=7,
$$

and write $C$ and $I$ for its clique and independent-set parts. For any vertex
subset $X$, put

$$
a=|X\cap C|,
\qquad
b=|X\cap I|.
$$

The clique vertices have degree $6$, and the independent-set vertices have
degree $r$. Consequently,

$$
\begin{aligned}
|\partial X|
  &=a(r-a)+a(s-b)+(r-a)b,\\
\operatorname{vol}(X)
  &=6a+rb,\\
\operatorname{vol}(V\setminus X)
  &=6(r-a)+r(s-b).
\end{aligned}
\tag{3}
$$

The cut ratio is unchanged when $(a,b)$ is replaced by
$(r-a,s-b)$. It therefore suffices to list one representative from each
complementary pair of nonempty proper cut types.

## The counterexample

Take

$$
G=F_{4,3}=K_4\vee E_3.
$$

Formula (3) gives the following complete list, where $m(X)$ denotes the
smaller of the two volumes:

$$
\begin{array}{c|c|c|c|c}
a&b&|\partial X|&m(X)&|\partial X|/m(X)\\
\hline
0&1&4&4&1\\
0&2&8&8&1\\
0&3&12&12&1\\
1&0&6&6&1\\
1&1&8&10&4/5\\
1&2&10&14&5/7\\
1&3&12&18&2/3\\
2&0&10&12&5/6\\
2&1&10&16&5/8
\end{array}
$$

Hence

$$
h(G)=\frac58.
\tag{4}
$$

On the other hand, the proposed seven-vertex extremal graph is

$$
H=F_{3,4}=K_3\vee E_4.
$$

Its complete list of complementary cut types is

$$
\begin{array}{c|c|c|c|c}
a&b&|\partial X|&m(X)&|\partial X|/m(X)\\
\hline
0&1&3&3&1\\
0&2&6&6&1\\
0&3&9&9&1\\
0&4&12&12&1\\
1&0&6&6&1\\
1&1&7&9&7/9\\
1&2&8&12&2/3\\
1&3&9&15&3/5\\
1&4&10&12&5/6
\end{array}
$$

Therefore

$$
h(H)=\frac35.
\tag{5}
$$

The graph $G$ is neither a star nor a complete graph. Its complement is

$$
G^c=E_4\sqcup K_3,
$$

which is disconnected, so $h(G^c)=0$. Combining (4) and (5),

$$
\boxed{
\max\bigl\{h(G),h(G^c)\bigr\}
=\frac58
>\frac35
=h\bigl(K_3\vee E_4\bigr).
}
$$

Thus the conjectured bound is false. In particular, the proposed extremizer is
not maximal even among seven-vertex generalized stars. The disconnected
complement is permitted by the conjecture as stated; indeed, the proposed
extremizer itself has disconnected complement.
